 Order

This petition filed under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure (for short, 'the Cr.P.C.') is by sole accused with a prayer to release him in Crime No.79/2023 of Byadagi Police Station for the offences punishable u/secs.306, 504 and 506 IPC.
2.
In support of the petition, petitioner has contended that he is innocent, law abiding and peace loving citizen.
He has not committed the alleged offences.
He has been falsely implicated.
There is no prima facie material to connect him with the alleged crime.
The allegations made in the complaint does not attract the provisions of Section 306 IPC.
Since the complainant and deceased were not having children, deceased was depressed.
For this reason, he has committed suicide.
Petitioner has nothing to do with the same.
Petitioner is coming from a respectable family owning moveable and immoveable properties.
The alleged offences are not exclusively punishable with death or life imprisonment for NC: 2023:KHC-D:9130 life.
He is ready and willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and prays to allow the petition.

3. Learned High Court Government Pleader submitted oral objections stating that the petitioner is already convicted in S.C.No.41/2016 on the file of II Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Haveri sitting at Ranebennur for the offences punishable u/secs.376, 323, 506 IPC.

sentences.text: He has filed Criminal Appeal No.100016/2019 wherein his sentence is suspended.
After availing bail, he is involved in the present case.

3.1 Learned HCGP would further submit that based on the complaint filed by Smt.Chandrakala wife of deceased Kuberappa, the present case is registered for the offences punishable u/secs. 306, 504 and 506 IPC.
The complaint discloses that complainant and deceased were married about fifteen years back.
Deceased was having four brothers and all of them are living separately.
Petitioner was in the habit of visiting the house of brother of deceased namely Subhash during his absence and it NC: 2023:KHC-D:9130 was objected by Subhash.

About two months prior to the date of incident,
petitioner misbehaved with the wife of Subhash namely Nirmala and in this connection Subhash assaulted him and brought him before the village elders and they warned him not to visit the house of Subhash.
3.2 Despite the same, petitioner was in the habit of visiting his house during his absence.
In this background since from 04.05.2023, Subhash has left the house and his whereabouts are not known.
In this regard, a missing compliant has been filed.
On the date of election under the pretext of casting his vote, petitioner visited village and started going to the house of Subhash.
When deceased Muranagouda came to know about it, he confronted the petitioner for which petitioner reacted him by abusing him in filthy language and gave threat to his life.

sentences.text: tremendous stress and he was fearful of his life.
He was also insulted by the fact that the petitioner was visiting the house of Subhash.

Though he was advised, he did not stop worrying about NC:
2023:KHC-D:9130 the threat given by the petitioner and ultimately on 12.05.2023, he committed suicide by jumping into the pond.
3.3
Based on the complaint, case is registered and investigation is taken up.
After completing the investigation, charge sheet is filed against the petitioner for the offences punishable u/secs.306, 504 and 506 IPC.
It make out a prima facie case.
If released on bail, there is likelihood of petitioner tampering with the prosecution witnesses and also involve in similar offences and prays to reject the petition.

4. Heard arguments and perused the record.
5.

As evident from the complaint averments as well as the charge sheet filed against the petitioner,
the petitioner is in the habit of acting highhandedly.
Though objected to by the brother of deceased namely Subhash as well as deceased, he was visiting the house of Subhash and meeting his wife Nirmala.
In this background, NC: 2023:KHC-D:9130 petitioner was once assaulted by Subhash and though he was advised by the village elders, he did not stop visiting his house.
Infact, Subhash has left the house and he is missing and his whereabouts are not known.
In this background, when the deceased also objected the petitioner from going to the house of Subhash and meeting his wife, he has given threat of dire consequences.
In this background, the deceased has chosen to end his life by jumping into the pond.

6. Though it is pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the postmortem report reveal that at the time of committing suicide, deceased had consumed alcohol, whether the deceased committed suicide on the instigation and abatement of the petitioner is a matter to be decided at the trial.

Already the petitioner is convicted for the offences punishable u/secs. 376, 323, 506 IPC and the appeal filed by him is pending before this Court in Criminal Appeal No.100016/2019 and after securing order of suspension of sentence and bail, once again petitioner is NC: 2023:KHC-D:9130 involved in the present offence.
Looking to the conduct of the petitioner, it cannot be ruled out that there is possibility of he threatening and tampering with the witnesses and also involving in similar offences.

For these reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioner is not entitled for bail and accordingly, the following:
ORDER Petition filed U/sec.439 Cr.P.C. is rejected.
